comment: Agent-style layout tasks: a real board is stripped to what an agent starts from (tracks removed, movable footprints stacked at one point, optionally no outline), then laid out from constraints. expected_misses lists constraints that are geometrically impossible (documented in the task's notes); a task passes when every other constraint holds, every connection is routed and KiCad reports no copper error.

tasks.name: hierarchy-from-netlist
tasks.notes: KiCad's complex-hierarchy demo from a netlist: board size, connectors on the left and right edges, a decoupling capacitor at its amplifier, a ground plane on the top (the bottom has one).

tasks.name: esp32-dut-from-netlist
tasks.notes: The ESP32-C3 test board: the controller module on the left edge, the device under test on the right, service headers on top, the system header along the bottom, decoupling next to each module.

tasks.name: esp-usb-corner
tasks.notes: The breadboard fence's USB/ESP corner (benchmarks/fence/esp-usb-placement): module flush in the corner with its antenna beyond the top edge, USB-C below it opening outwards. C5/C6 cannot come within 6 mm of the module's pin 3 (the pad sits 8.4 mm inside its courtyard), and J4 cannot sit within 3 mm below the module with C5/C6 in between.
